transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in today?

Hi, Dr. [Name]. Um, thank you for seeing me. I hope I'm not taking up too much of your time. I... well, I guess I'm here because I've been having some trouble with my eating lately? It's probably not a huge deal, but sometimes, especially after a long day of teaching and grading papers, I just... I end up eating a bit more than I probably should. 

Like, I'll start with some leftovers, and then maybe I'll have a little cereal, and then some crackers... and before I know it, I've kind of gone through the peanut butter and even the snacks I keep for my students. It's just... it happens sometimes, and it kind of scares me a little bit, how much I can eat in one sitting. Is that... does that make sense? I mean, I know everyone overeats sometimes, right?
When you find yourself eating more than you intended, do you feel like you can't stop or control what you're doing at the time?

Um... yeah, I think that's exactly it. I hope it doesn't sound too strange, but... once I start, it almost feels like the reasonable, teacher part of me is just kind of watching from the outside? Like she's standing there saying, 'Joan, you really should stop now.' 

But... my hands just keep opening wrappers and boxes anyway. I just keep putting food in my mouth until I'm... well, until I'm really painfully full. I know I shouldn't let it get to that point, and I try so hard to be good, I really do. Does that make sense? I'm sure you hear things like that a lot, right?
